reason: The iron-bearing fraction needs separating first, but the board does not show a magnet or separator. Inspecting the screened regolith should reveal how to proceed.
expectation: The compatibility list should identify an available way to process or separate the feedstock.

alternatives.reason: The retort may reveal its connections, but separation comes first.

effect: The screened regolith has no available operation yet, so some preparation must come first.
reaction: That is consistent with needing to separate the iron-bearing fraction, though the separator is not obvious.
reason: The unconnected retort likely needs power before it can process material.
expectation: The cable should connect power to the retort, leaving any other required connections to be made.

alternatives.reason: Checking its available connections would be safer if the cable is not enough.

effect: The cable and steel made a powered magnetic separator, providing the missing way to isolate the iron-bearing fraction.
reaction: The automatic correction was useful; I hadn't recognized the cable as coil material.
reason: The separator should extract the magnetic fraction from the screened regolith.
expectation: The magnet will separate iron-bearing grains from the screened feedstock.

effect: The magnetic separator produced iron-rich concentrate, ready for the retort once it is connected.
reaction: The distinction between the assay and the soil's red colour was useful.
reason: The retort needs the hydrogen outlet to reduce the iron-bearing material.
expectation: The retort will connect to the hydrogen supply, preparing it to process the concentrate.

effect: The retort now has heat and a hydrogen connection, and its liner is ready for the concentrate.
reaction: The contained exhaust and condensate make the processing setup feel more credible.
reason: The iron-rich concentrate is the feedstock the connected retort is prepared to process.
expectation: Heating the concentrate with hydrogen should yield usable iron or an intermediate that can be formed into it.

effect: Hydrogen reduction produced porous, weak iron sponge that now needs forming at the press.
reaction: The distinction between reduced metal and usable formed iron is helpful.
reason: The process carrier has brought the iron sponge to the workshop press, making pressing the clear next step.
expectation: The press should compact the porous sponge into a usable iron form.

effect: The heated press consolidated the sponge into a dense iron billet, completing the iron-making goal and revealing the need for a process frame.
reaction: The separate consolidation step clarified why simply pressing the weak sponge was not enough.
reason: The fuel-fab footing is the available site for the process equipment, and the consolidated iron can be shaped into its frame.
expectation: The iron will be shaped into a process frame on the prepared footing.

effect: The press shaped the billet into iron bars and brackets, which can now serve as non-pressure supports for the process frame.
reaction: The automatic correction clarified that the billet needed shaping before installation.
reason: The bars and brackets are suited to building the process frame on the prepared fuel-fab footing.
expectation: The supports will be assembled into a process frame on the footing.

effect: The shaped iron supports became a process frame on the footing, completing the chapter’s goals.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the local material become a support for the gas installation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reducing the concentrate and consolidating the iron was most worthwhile: the separate steps made clear why porous reduced metal is not yet a usable billet.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the screened regolith was the least useful decision: it had no available operation until the separator was made.

surprise.text: I had not recognized the power cable as material for an electromagnet. The correction revealed a physically sensible way to separate the feedstock.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt wholly arbitrary, though needing the press again to shape the billet before installation was not obvious to me until the automatic correction.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the locally made frame supports the return-fuel installation; the material-processing details made the construction interesting.
